THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the appellant- Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 05.11.2011 passed in MVC.No.6797/2008 by III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-18), on the ground that the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-K-9063 is falsely implicated into the case.
NC: 2023:KHC:21212 2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The factum of accident is not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.
Learned counsel for the appellant- Insurance Company submitted that the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-K-9063 was falsely implicated into the case.
The accident was caused on 13.04.2008, but the complaint was lodged on 09.05.2008.

Therefore, there is a delay of 26 days in The Branch Manager vs Sri S D Thulasidas on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119745388/
2 lodging the complaint, for which, there is no explanation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, quite naturally, when there is a delay of 26 days in lodging the complaint, the vehicle must have been implicated by mentioning the vehicle number in the complaint.
Therefore, submitted that, in this regard, offending motor cycle is falsely implicated into the case.
Hence, prays to allow the appeal by setting aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1-claimant justified the judgment and NC:
2023:KHC:21212 award passed by the Tribunal.
Therefore, prays to dismiss the appeal.
6. In the present case, it is stated that the accident was caused on 13.04.2008.
It is stated that immediately after the accident, the claimant was shifted to Sarvodaya Hospital, Bangalore, for treatment.
The claimant was admitted in the said hospital as inpatient till 20.04.2008 and on that day, the claimant was discharged.
But the complaint is lodged on 09.05.2008.

Therefore, even after discharge from the hospital, there is a delay of 21 days in lodging the complaint before the police,
quite naturally, all the police records such as registration of FIR, spot sketch, motor vehicle accident report are all subsequent to filing of the complaint before the police.
In motor vehicle accident report also, the offending motor vehicle is not inspected.

There is no evidence on record that the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-K- 9063 was seized and produced before the motor vehicle Inspector for inspection, but only the claimant's motor NC: 2023:KHC:21212 cycle was seized and inspected.
Therefore, the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-K-9063 was not seized and was not inspected.
Even on the medical records, it is only stated that the claimant had sustained injuries in the road traffic accident.

At the most, it is proved that the claimant might have sustained injuries in the road traffic accident, but for proving that this motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-K-9063 was involved, absolutely there is no evidence, since there is a delay of 26 days in lodging the complaint from the date of the accident and quite naturally, all the police records are subsequent to lodging of complaint, but there is no evidence regarding involvement of the offending motor cycle.

7. Under these facts and circumstances and evidence on record, the reason assigned by the Tribunal in the judgment regarding involvement of the offending motor cycle is not correct as it is perverse to the evidence on record.
Therefore, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 05.11.2011 passed in MVC.No.6797/2008 by the III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore (SCCH-18) is hereby set aside.
